articles.summary: Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now help develop many models published as general solutions. articles.title: Motion-Aware Reward Modeling for Instruction-Guided Video Editing
articles.summary: Reward models for instruction-guided video editing can favor temporal consistency at the expense of motion. We study this failure, termed motion collapse, using controlled motion-suppression variants of real edits. articles.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
articles.summary: Intent contracts are an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. For each step it submits a short logged contract: a goal, a verbatim quotation of the user, and scope fields. articles.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
articles.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. articles.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
articles.summary: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. articles.summary: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. articles.title: Non-penetrating World Models
articles.summary: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. articles.summary: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extends residual connections to multiple streams and stabilizes residual propagation by constraining stream-mixing residual matrices to the Birkhoff polytope, the set of doubly stochastic matrices. articles.title: Explicit Style Extraction for Personalized Long-Form Text Generation
articles.summary: Personalized long-form generation asks a language model to write new text the way a specific user would. The standard recipe, retrieval-augmented generation, places a few of the user's past texts in the prompt but leaves the model to decide what to take from them. articles.summary: Text-aware image super-resolution (TAISR) aims to recover high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs while preserving textual content. articles.summary: Prompt enhancement (PE) refines concise user prompts into detailed descriptions to improve the compositional aesthetics of generated images while preserving user intent. articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. articles.title: Lost in the Hallway: Benchmarking Persistent Spatial Memory Across Revisits
articles.summary: Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents to operate reliably in environments they repeatedly encounter. It requires recognizing revisited places despite viewpoint changes, distinguishing them from similar-looking rooms, and updating memories as environments change. articles.summary: Identity matching asks whether two records denote the same identity, yet the answer depends on the target granularity. articles.summary: Learning and inference on time series can pose significant statistical challenges, including autocorrelated observations, distribution shift over time, and the curse of dimensionality. articles.title: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models to Stop Safely
articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. articles.summary: End-to-end autonomous driving increasingly depends on scaling training demonstrations, yet data growth does not guarantee proportional gains. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. articles.summary: Agentic artificial intelligence could automate analyses of sensitive clinical data, but current agents depend on large language models (LLMs). Cloud LLMs expose patient data. articles.summary: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. articles.summary: Recently, video world models have advanced interactive generation, with large models offering higher quality and smaller models enabling faster inference. articles.summary: Native 3D generation has largely been built around latent diffusion, with recent advances concentrating on stronger variational autoencoders (VAE) and increasingly elaborate latent representations, from vecset and triplanes to structured sparse voxels. articles.summary: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. articles.summary: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. articles.summary: A direction in a language model's hidden state can be used to probe whether a concept is present or to steer the model toward it. Although probe directions are often reused for steering, the direction that best detects a concept need not be the one that best changes it. articles.title: Training Vision Models for LLM-Driven Weight-Space Programming

articles.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges and graders to replace human annotators, raising the question of when such replacement is statistically justified. articles.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning

articles.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
articles.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. articles.summary: Unified multimodal models aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single framework. articles.summary: World models aim to predict environment dynamics under actions, enabling the prediction of action consequences without executing them in the real world. articles.summary: Code-search benchmarks show dense encoders well ahead of BM25, yet coding agents do well with grep. What does this dense advantage measure?
